subject.title: Feature Request: Add custom client display name for TUI

question: Should OpenClaw expose a user-facing TUI display-name override, and if so should it be a CLI-only `--client-name` flag, a persisted config setting, or an auto-derived label?
rationale: This adds a public CLI/config-adjacent surface and changes Gateway-visible presence identity metadata, so automation should not choose naming, persistence, or privacy defaults without maintainer intent.

options.title: Add CLI-only opt-in flag
options.body: Add a bounded `openclaw tui --client-name <name>` path that only affects Gateway-mode presence for that process and keeps the existing default unchanged.

options.title: Add persisted TUI config
options.body: Add a `tui` config key if maintainers want a stable per-user default, with schema/docs/tests and no upgrade surprise for existing users.

options.title: Decline or defer
options.body: Keep `openclaw-tui` as the only TUI label until a broader TUI identity/privacy policy is decided.

recommendation.title: Add CLI-only opt-in flag
recommendation.body: Add a bounded `openclaw tui --client-name <name>` path that only affects Gateway-mode presence for that process and keeps the existing default unchanged.

likelyOwner.reason: This handle has the strongest history on both the original Gateway TUI path and the current `openclaw-tui` label, and the blocker is product/API shape.
